messages.text: How does ColBERT score a passage?

statements.text: ColBERT encodes the query and the passage into one vector per token.
It scores with a sum of maximum similarities over query tokens.
ColBERT is ten times more accurate than BERT re-rankers.

messages.text: Is ColBERT faster than a BERT cross-encoder?

statements.text: ColBERT precomputes passage embeddings offline.
Re-ranking with ColBERT is two orders of magnitude faster than BERT.

messages.text: Does it beat BM25 everywhere?

statements.text: ColBERT beats BM25 on every BEIR dataset.

messages.text: What does BEIR measure?

statements.text: BEIR is a benchmark of 18 retrieval datasets for zero-shot evaluation.
BM25 is a strong baseline across BEIR datasets.
Dense retrievers always beat BM25 on BEIR.

messages.text: Why does BEIR disagree with ColBERT's MS MARCO results?

statements.text: Models tuned on MS MARCO can generalise poorly to other domains.
Late-interaction models like ColBERT generalised better than dense single-vector models in BEIR.

messages.text: So which one should I use for biomedical search?
What is DensePhrases?

statements.text: DensePhrases indexes phrases as dense vectors for retrieval.
It answers open-domain questions by retrieving phrases directly.
DensePhrases needs no training data at all.

messages.text: Can DensePhrases retrieve passages, not just phrases?

statements.text: Phrase retrieval can be turned into passage retrieval by taking the passage that holds the top phrase.
It outperforms DPR on passage retrieval for all datasets.

messages.text: How was CLIP trained?

statements.text: CLIP learns from 400 million image-text pairs.
It trains an image encoder and a text encoder with a contrastive objective.
CLIP was trained on ImageNet labels.

messages.text: Can CLIP classify images it was not trained on?

statements.text: CLIP does zero-shot classification by comparing an image with text prompts for each class.
Zero-shot CLIP matches a supervised ResNet-50 on ImageNet.

messages.text: What about counting objects?

statements.text: CLIP is very good at counting objects.

messages.text: What is instruction tuning in FLAN?

statements.text: FLAN fine-tunes a language model on many tasks phrased as instructions.
Instruction tuning improves zero-shot performance on unseen tasks.

messages.text: Does instruction tuning help small models?

statements.text: The benefit of instruction tuning appears only at larger model scales.
Instruction tuning helps every model size equally.

messages.text: I need to read the ablation on number of task clusters later.
What is MTEB?

statements.text: MTEB is a benchmark of text embedding models over many tasks.
No single embedding model wins on every MTEB task.
SGPT wins every MTEB task.

messages.text: What does XTR change about ColBERT?

statements.text: XTR trains the model to retrieve the most important document tokens first.
This removes the gathering stage of multi-vector retrieval.
XTR is a cross-encoder.

messages.text: How does DPR retrieve passages?

statements.text: DPR uses two BERT encoders, one for questions and one for passages.
It retrieves by inner product between the two embeddings.

messages.text: Is it better than BM25?

statements.text: DPR beats BM25 by 9 to 19 points top-20 accuracy on several QA datasets.

messages.text: What is SPLADE?

statements.text: SPLADE learns sparse lexical representations with term expansion.
SPLADE needs a GPU at query time for an inverted index.

messages.text: What does the Visual Spatial Reasoning dataset test?

statements.text: VSR tests whether models understand spatial relations between objects in images.
Vision-language models perform far below humans on VSR.
Models reach human accuracy on VSR.

messages.text: Is there a newer version of ColBERT that uses less storage?

statements.text: ColBERT stores one vector per token, which takes a lot of space.

messages.text: I want to find out how ColBERTv2 compresses the index.
Which retriever is best for code search?

statements.text: ColBERT is the best retriever for code search.
BM25 cannot handle code at all.

messages.text: Compare CLIP and FLAN briefly.

statements.text: CLIP aligns images and text with contrastive learning.
FLAN is instruction-tuned on many NLP tasks.
CLIP and FLAN were trained on the same data.
